heading_path: Scheduled workflows running at unexpected times
hits.tldr: Scheduled workflows may delay during high-load periods, especially at the start of each hour.
The actor for scheduled workflows changes when repository events occur, like default branch changes or cron schedule edits by authorized users.
The schedule event triggers GitHub Actions workflows at specified times using cron syntax.
Manually re-running a Dependabot workflow maintains original privileges regardless of who initiates the rerun.
GitHub Actions sends notifications when triggered workflows complete, with status details and user-based routing for scheduled workflows.

{"heading_path":["schedule","actor for scheduled workflows"],"line_end":995,"line_start":983,"rel_path":"content/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows.md","requested_id":"e3d06046eb1408e6#42","section_id":"e3d06046eb1408e6#42","stale":false,"text":"### `actor` for scheduled workflows

Certain repository events change the `actor` associated with the workflow. For example, a user who changes the default branch of the repository, which changes the branch on which scheduled workflows run, becomes `actor` for those scheduled workflows.

For a deactivated scheduled workflow, if a user with `write` permissions to the repository makes a commit that changes the `cron` schedule on the workflow, the workflow will be reactivated, and that user will become the `actor` associated with any workflow runs.

Notifications for scheduled workflows are sent to the user who last modified the cron syntax in the workflow file. For more information, see [AUTOTITLE](/actions/concepts/workflows-and-actions/notifications-for-workflow-runs).

> [!NOTE]
> For an enterprise with {% data variables.product.prodname_emus %}, triggering a scheduled workflow requires that the status of the `actor` user account associated with the workflow is currently active (i.e. not suspended or deleted).
> * Scheduled workflows will not run if the last `actor` associated with the scheduled workflow has been deprovisioned by the {% data variables.product.prodname_emu %} identity provider (IdP). However, if the last `actor` {% data variables.product.prodname_emu %} has not been deprovisioned by the IdP, and has only been removed as a member from a given organization in the enterprise, scheduled workflows will still run with that user set as the `actor`.
> * Similarly, for an enterprise without {% data variables.product.prodname_emus %}, removing a user from an organization will not prevent scheduled workflows which had that user as their `actor` from running.
> * Thus, the _user account's_ status, in both {% data variables.product.prodname_emu %} and non-{% data variables.product.prodname_emu %} scenarios, is what's important, _not_ the user's _membership status_ in the organization where the scheduled workflow is located."}

structuredContent.text:
### `actor` for scheduled workflows

Certain repository events change the `actor` associated with the workflow. For example, a user who changes the default branch of the repository, which changes the branch on which scheduled workflows run, becomes `actor` for those scheduled workflows.

For a deactivated scheduled workflow, if a user with `write` permissions to the repository makes a commit that changes the `cron` schedule on the workflow, the workflow will be reactivated, and that user will become the `actor` associated with any workflow runs.

Notifications for scheduled workflows are sent to the user who last modified the cron syntax in the workflow file. For more information, see [AUTOTITLE](/actions/concepts/workflows-and-actions/notifications-for-workflow-runs).

> [!NOTE]
> For an enterprise with {% data variables.product.prodname_emus %}, triggering a scheduled workflow requires that the status of the `actor` user account associated with the workflow is currently active (i.e. not suspended or deleted).
> * Scheduled workflows will not run if the last `actor` associated with the scheduled workflow has been deprovisioned by the {% data variables.product.prodname_emu %} identity provider (IdP). However, if the last `actor` {% data variables.product.prodname_emu %} has not been deprovisioned by the IdP, and has only been removed as a member from a given organization in the enterprise, scheduled workflows will still run with that user set as the `actor`.
> * Similarly, for an enterprise without {% data variables.product.prodname_emus %}, removing a user from an organization will not prevent scheduled workflows which had that user as their `actor` from running.
> * Thus, the _user account's_ status, in both {% data variables.product.prodname_emu %} and non-{% data variables.product.prodname_emu %} scenarios, is what's important, _not_ the user's _membership status_ in the organization where the scheduled workflow is located.

content.text:
This is documented behavior, not a bug.

Per `content/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows.md` (§ "schedule" → "actor for scheduled workflows", lines 983-995): the `actor` for a scheduled workflow is whoever last modified the cron syntax. If that user's account is deactivated/suspended/deleted, scheduled workflows tied to that actor stop running — this is explicitly called out for EMU orgs and applies analogously to a deleted personal account. Removing a user from an org alone doesn't stop it — only the account itself being deprovisioned/deleted does.

There's no mention in the docs of an automatic warning/email being sent to other repo maintainers in that case, so your feature request for a notification isn't currently covered — you'd want to file that as a suggestion (e.g. via GitHub Community/feedback), not something addressed in these docs.
